newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince buys stake in Beirut finance house.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince buys stake in Beirut finance house.

text.p: Saudi businessman Prince al-Waleed bin Talal has become a major partner in Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest (LI) after buying an undisclosed number of shares, a statement from the prince said on Monday.

The statement faxed to Reuters by the Riyadh-based United Saudi Commercial Bank -- chaired by Prince Waleed -- said the purchase reflected the prince's "desire to help rebuild Lebanon, develop its economy and take part in vital projects carried out by LI."
The statement gave no further details and the billionaire prince, whose global interests include stakes in U.S. banking giant Citicorp and Euro Disney, was not available for comment.
The London-based al-Hayat newspaper said the prince's stake in LI now stood at seven percent.
LI said late last month it would increase its capital by $13.75 million to $40 million through a private share placement that would close at the beginning of March.
The capital increase, decided by a shareholders' assembly in mid-December, will come from four million new shareholders and nine million existing shareholders.
The existing shareholders include Prince Waleed who took a "small stake" in the bank in December.
